title: All things new (Apocalypse 21:1–5)
hook: God shall wipe away every tear
carry: behold, I make all things new

segments.voice: Yesterday, alleluia, a wedding, and cenam Agni, the supper of the Lamb. Your line was called to the supper.

A kid falls off a bike. Scraped knee, gravel in the palm, a howl you can hear three houses away. A parent comes running and, before the bandage, before anything, takes the child's face in both hands and wipes the tears off with a thumb. You have to be very close to do it. Near the end of the Apocalypse, after the dragon and the beasts and Babylon, John says God will do exactly that.
screen: `A SCRAPED KNEE ON THE SIDEWALK.` → `A THUMB ACROSS A WET CHEEK.` → `GOD WILL DO EXACTLY THAT.`

segments.voice: Chapter twenty-one opens, in the Douay-Rheims: "And I saw a new heaven and a new earth." And the sea is no more. Some readers hear the sea as a picture of chaos, and John, remember, was on an island, cut off by water. Then: "And I John saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband." Notice the direction. The city comes down. The story doesn't end with people escaping earth; it ends with heaven coming to earth. A great voice says: "Behold the tabernacle of God with men, and he will dwell with them." The Greek word behind tabernacle means a tent: God pitching his tent among his people, the same image John's Gospel uses when the Word became flesh and dwelt among us. Catholics also call the place in church where the Eucharist is kept the tabernacle. Then: "And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes: and death shall be no more, nor mourning, nor crying, nor sorrow shall be any more, for the former things are passed away." Not prevent the tears: wipe them. They were real. Then the one on the throne speaks: "Behold, I make all things new." Not all new things, a replacement world with the old one thrown out. All things, made new. The Catechism teaches that the universe itself will be renewed, not discarded. The Church offers this among the readings at funerals, to families whose tears haven't been wiped yet.
screen: `A NEW HEAVEN AND A NEW EARTH.` · `THE CITY COMES DOWN.` · `GOD PITCHES HIS TENT WITH US.` · `NOT ALL NEW THINGS: ALL THINGS NEW.` · then, large: `GOD SHALL WIPE AWAY ALL TEARS.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who is crying right now, or sad a long time, and picture yourself kneeling close beside them, gently wiping their face. If there's a sorrow of your own, let someone do the same for you; you can even touch your own cheek with your thumb. If you pray, rest in the promise, God shall wipe away all tears; if not, just let the gentleness stay.
Tabernacle, a tent. Apocalypse twenty-one: God pitching his tent among his people, in the new Jerusalem come down to earth. Today's word.

Your line: behold, I make all things new. And that's week ninety: they rest not, worthy is the lamb, every tongue, clothed with the sun, what doesn't last, called to the supper, and all things new. Ninety weeks in.

howItsDone: Apocalypse 21 is among the readings families may choose for a Catholic funeral Mass, and the Church teaches that at the end of time the whole universe will be renewed, with God dwelling among his people.

original.note: Greek: I make all things new (Apocalypse 21:5). kainos means new in kind, fresh.

trapdoor: what you thought: heaven is somewhere else, far away from this world.
what it means: heaven comes down; God dwells with his people; this world, renewed, with every tear wiped away.
what a scholar hears: kainos, new in quality, not just in time; and skēnē, tent, God pitching his tent with us, as in John 1:14.
recall: a crowd from every nation and tongue

chat.says: What does 'I make all things new' mean? A brand-new world?
options: Not new things replacing old: all things made new. The city comes down to earth.
It means each person gets a new body the moment they're baptized.
It means God starts each year fresh, so old sins no longer count.
chat.meaning: Behold, I make all things new: not a replacement world, but all things renewed. The new Jerusalem comes down, and God dwells with his people.

tabernacle.meaning: a tent; also where the Eucharist is kept in church

new Jerusalem.meaning: the holy city John sees coming down from heaven
